explanation: Salt lowers the freezing point of water, so the melting brine drops well below 0 °C and pulls heat out of the cream fast enough to freeze it.

claims.text: Hand-cranked ice-cream makers surround the churn with a mixture of ice and coarse rock salt.
Sugar, sand and vinegar are not mixed with the ice around the churn.
Salt lowers the freezing point of water, so an ice and salt brine gets much colder than plain melting ice.
The brine falls well below 0 °C, which freezes the cream mixture.
